composers_checked.name: Fiorillo, Federigo
composers_checked.note: Grove (via Da Vinci Classics) dates his first Paris publications to 1785–88, so Op. 4 is c. 1785–88; year left blank. Only the Op. 4 flute quartets are recorded (Tactus 2008; Da Vinci Classics). Gap check against Wikipedia/Fétis list (Opp. 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 12, 16 and a quintet for horn, flute, violin, viola and bass): nothing else recorded. Op. 36 on IMSLP is an arrangement of Pleyel.

composers_checked.name: Campagnoli, Bartolomeo
composers_checked.note: Both sets recorded complete (string quartets: Ensemble Symposium, Brilliant 2014, from the Berlin manuscript; flute quartets: Brilliant 2018, Tactus 2012, Ferrarini). Numbering and keys follow the recordings; the flute-quartet keys match the IMSLP list, the string-quartet keys are not given on IMSLP (same Berlin manuscript as the recording). Gap check against Wikipedia (it/de/en) and Apple Music: the rest of his output is duos, solo violin and viola studies and concertos; nothing in scope missing.

composers_checked.name: Nardini, Pietro
composers_checked.note: Floor from Apple Music track lists: quartets by Quartetto Eleusi (Brilliant 2013), trio sonatas, the A-major sonata and the 14 minuets by Violini Capricciosi (Brilliant 2023). Gap check against Wikipedia (it/de), Grove summary and the recordings: added the A-major trio sonata (IMSLP page outside the census) and the minuets. Five trios with flute (Musicaphon 2010) not added: scoring unconfirmed.

note: Fiorillo: only the six flute quartets Op. 4 are recorded (Tactus, Ensemble a l'Antica; Da Vinci Classics, Il Furibondo/Narcisi); keys C, A, G, F, D, E minor match IMSLP's Sieber print; every other Fiorillo page skipped as not performed or recorded. Not added: the Quintet for horn, flute (oboe), violin, viola and bass (Sieber c. 1789, published under Punto's name; corno.de edition ROM 046) - no commercial recording found. Campagnoli: both sets are manuscripts (string quartets Berlin SBB, flute quartets Copenhagen); the numbering and keys follow the complete recordings (the flute-quartet keys match the IMSLP list; IMSLP gives no keys for the string quartets, whose recording uses the same Berlin manuscript); no opus numbers or dates confirmed, so year is blank. Nardini: quartet numbering and keys follow the Quartetto Eleusi recording (Florence print, 1782); I did not check that Altmann's IMSLP edition uses the same order. The 1768 trio sonatas print reads 'for two German Flutes or two Violins and a Bass'; kept with violins (recorded with violins, and a flute-only scoring would leave no string part), flutes in alternatives. Gap additions: Trio Sonata in A major (IMSLP page by G. Bracci, 2026, outside the census) and the Fourteen New Italian Minuets (only Minuet No. 2 is on IMSLP, as its own page), both recorded on Brilliant 96873. Open: 'Kammermusik mit Flöte' (Musica Solare, Darja Großheide, Musicaphon 2010) holds five 'Flute Trios' (C, G, C, G, C), said by a retailer to be for flute, violin and continuo; not added because the scoring could not be confirmed from a page I opened. Concertos (Op. 1, the D-major concerto a quattro) stay out as orchestra/string orchestra. Levels are estimates without score study (medium confidence).
